note: Re-judged 2026-11-20 by an independent agent after the row gained a {partial} annotation, replacing this agent's earlier enforced verdict, which had left the ICMPv6 case as a residual. RFC 4301 Section 6: "Disposition of non-error, ICMP messages (that are not addressed to the IPsec implementation itself) MUST be explicitly accounted for using SPD entries." and "The discussion in this section applies to ICMPv6 as well as to ICMPv4." Tested: "MUST be explicitly accounted for using SPD entries"; Gap: "Disposition of non-error, ICMP messages", split by case: the transit ICMPv6 non-error message. Producer: internal/component/ike/engine/spd_policy.go::spdTransitPolicies, the first path::Symbol in the reason. It is the right producer for the bypass: it builds the FWD decision and the transit gates that carry a forwarded Echo, and the gate the negative's discard must out-rank. The tested scope is enforced. Positive, TestRFC4301OperatorBypassForwardsTransitEchoInClear: under `unmatched discard` with no Child SA, a transit Echo Request (not addressed to Ze) is first not forwarded in either direction while no operator entry names it; then a both-direction operator BYPASS for ICMP, accepted by verifySPDOrder, installed through installSPDPolicies and read back from the kernel (transitWantInstalled, which also requires a forward policy), forwards a second Echo in each direction, seen in clear on the egress link. The entry is the only change between the two observations. Negative, TestRFC4301ForwardedICMPErrorUnderOperatorDiscardMapsToReturnSA, Echo case: an operator out DISCARD for ICMP, with an in BYPASS whose OUT transit gate would otherwise carry the Echo in clear, gives XfrmOutPolBlock +1 and no copy at the peer, protected or in clear. The gap is honest: every case is IPv4, and AC-8 of plan/release/validation/spec-ipsec-fragment-receive-and-kernel-proof.md names RFC4301-6-1's ICMPv6 pair. Wording finding, not a scope defect: the reason says the first paragraph of Section 6 applies the section to ICMPv6, but that sentence is the second paragraph (the first ends "using SPD entries."); the 6.2-3, -4 and -5 reasons say the same. Record finding: every 6-1 record breaks spdTransitPolicies by a panic, which proves reachability only, and the discard test still holds a positive record for a polarity it no longer claims.
